angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 431,334 km at 76.46 pc = 0.08 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 13.0780 +/- 0.0145 mas (same row, RUWE 1.07): 76.46 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.62 +/- 0.02 solar radii from Díez Alonso et al. 2019, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-286 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.489.5928D/abstract): 431,334 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.64 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Díez Alonso et al. 2019, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-286 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.489.5928D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3926 +/- 100 K from Díez Alonso et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-286 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.489.5928D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Díez Alonso et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-286 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019MNRAS.489.5928D/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-286.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.659, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
